summary: ```markdown # Some Tips for Creating Pleats in Marvelous Designer ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will explore various techniques for creating pleats in Marvelous Designer. We will examine the properties of different panels and how they affect the simulation of pleats. ## Project Overview Open the project, and you will notice different shapes and properties of the panels. The particles also vary slightly across the panels. ## Simulating the Bottom Row of Panels First, let's simulate the bottom row of the panels. Observe that the wrinkles of the panels differ: - **First Row:** The wrinkles are larger. - **Second Row:** The wrinkles are darker and more detailed. - **Third Row:** The wrinkles are more delicate and softer. Each panel's properties are generally the same, except for the last panel, which has smaller particles. ## Understanding Pleat Differences The top and bottom of the pleats are distinct and do not match. The last version features more pleats, resulting in a more detailed appearance. In general, the pleats of triangular and quadrilateral meshes are harder, while those of vertical meshes are more delicate. ## Simulation of Different Pleats Next, we will simulate various pleats. Since the pleats are smaller, I will switch to GPU simulation. As we proceed from left to right, you will see that the pleats gradually decrease in size. After starting the simulation, the largest diameter pleats have already been simulated, while the smallest diameter pleats are just beginning. Currently, there are only one or two pleats simulated. The bundled pleats that are not yet completed can be simulated as well. Be aware that some units may not be fully simulated, which can affect the overall performance. ### Recommendations for Particle Diameter The simulation speed slows down when the particle diameter is reduced to 3, resulting in excessive wrinkles. Therefore, it is advisable to keep the particle diameter between 10 and 5 during the usual production process. ## Impact of Fabric on Simulation The fabric of the panel significantly affects the simulation results. 1. **Fan-Shaped Panels:** The lengths of the two panels are not significantly different, leading to minimal wrinkles at the seam side. 2. **Fabric Properties:** The second panel is obviously softer and exhibits a more vertical feel because it uses a different fabric. By clicking on the fabric to check its physical properties, you can observe that the strength of the gold-plated sand and the diagonal line is relatively low. The smoothness of the fabric aids in reducing faults and allows for longer use. ## Analyzing Panel Composition The second and third panels exhibit differences in their properties. The direction of the texture on each panel is indicated by arrows, which symbolize the gold image. You can see that the texture of the longer part of the click is different from the shorter part, which resembles the gold image or the tail image. ### Fabric Stretchability Clicking on the physical properties of the fabric reveals that it is very easy to stretch. In comparison, the high strength of the sand creates a more vertical appearance, but the direction of the foot line remains upright. ## Factors Affecting Pleat Shape The main factors influencing the shape of the pleats include: - The arrangement of the grid - The ratio of particles - The properties of the fabric - The shape of the panel ## Demonstrating Pleating Effects of Different Panels ### Rectangular Panels Let’s first examine the pleating effect of rectangular panels. You will notice that the only difference among the rectangular panels from left to right is their width. The number of pleats remains consistent across the panels. From the seam side, the pleats are abundant and gradually become smaller and wider. A larger panel results in more pleats along the seam, while the overall pleats become narrower. ### Fan-Shaped Panels Now, let’s look at the simulation effect of fan-shaped panels. These panels include an additional triangle in the rectangular shape, which maintains the same length for the pleats. Adjusting the panel's position facilitates our simulation. Upon opening the simulation, we can see that the shape of the panel differs significantly from rectangular shapes. The pleats appear more regular, with each triangle forming a pleat. The rectangular part of the panel is more even, and the seam side is also more balanced. ### Creating Custom Panels To create such a panel, utilize the extension tool. Set the direction of the baseline line and open the panel immediately. This method allows for easier visualization in the scene. ## Conclusion The size of the panel will also affect the fold effect of the model. From different angles, you can observe that the folds are becoming larger and wider. This type of panel is ideal for upper sections, while the bottom remains wide with a loose structure. In examining other models, it is evident that larger panels yield more folds and creases. For panels that shorten yet feature numerous folds, a spiral panel is recommended for optimal results. ```
